claim: On layouts with more than 1200 cells (width times height) our side eats and splits much less from raw round 151 on while the opponent does not, on main and on v31; on layouts of 1200 cells or fewer there is no such step at round 151 and the same step comes at round 301.
how_to_count: Three counts. (1) Pearls, from the replays or rows.jsonl curves: for each game that reached raw round 200 with at least 20 of our dragons alive after round 150, pearls eaten by each side in rounds 101-150 and 151-200 (a pearl is credited to the side whose dragon's turn removed it); ratio = sum over games of the second window / sum of the first, per side, for big layouts (width*height > 1200: Around UNSW, Australia, Schooltime #1 and #2, Islands, Slithery Fight) and for the others; main and v31 separately (our_code). Also the number of games in which our ratio is below theirs, the ratio per layout, and for the other layouts the same with windows 201-300 and 301-400 (games reaching round 400 with at least 10 of ours alive after round 300). (2) Splits: dragonSplit events per side in raw rounds 125-149 and 150-174, games that reached round 175 with at least 20 of our dragons alive at the start of round 150; ratio second / first, pooled; and rounds 275-299 against 300-324 for games reaching round 325 with at least 10 of ours alive at the start of round 300. (3) Adjacent pearls: every turn start of a non-queen dragon at which a pearl lies on a tile next to its head (open edge or portal partner tile) that no dragon body is on, and at which not every such pearl has an enemy head within 2 tiles (wrapped Manhattan); left = that dragon removes no pearl during the turn; rate = left / turns per side in raw rounds 101-125, 126-150, 151-175, 176-199 on big layouts, and in 251-300 against 301-350 on the others. Zone split for rounds 151-199 on big layouts: the turn is inside when, for every such adjacent pearl, the wrapped Manhattan distance to the nearest head among the same-side dragons of that side's greatest length (the acting dragon left out) is 9 or less. Neighbour split (rounds 101-199, big layouts): the turn is near when, for every such adjacent pearl, the wrapped Manhattan distance to the nearest head of a same-side dragon strictly longer than the acting dragon is 9 or less; otherwise (farther, or no longer same-side dragon) not near.
